report.title: Anthropic confidentially files S-1 for IPO at $965B valuation
report.summary: Anthropic filed a confidential S-1 with the SEC on June 1, days after closing a $65B Series H at a $965B post-money valuation. The filing positions Anthropic to list in October 2026, potentially beating OpenAI (September target) to public markets — which matters because both companies will be competing for the same institutional capital in quick succession.

report.title: Microsoft Build 2026 ships full agent stack: WAF open-sourced, Foundry Agent Service GA, Project Polaris unveiled
report.summary: Build 2026 (June 2-3, San Francisco) delivered the Windows Agent Framework open-sourced under MIT, Azure AI Foundry Agent Service moving to GA by end of June, Copilot Workspace out of beta, and Project Polaris — Microsoft's own in-house coding model — set to replace GPT-4 Turbo in GitHub Copilot by August 2026. Builders on .NET or Python now have a full production-grade agent runtime without locking into OpenAI's stack.

report.title: OpenAI ships Codex role-specific plugins, Sites hosting preview, and Annotations on June 2
report.summary: OpenAI expanded Codex with six role-specific plugins bundling 62 apps and 110 skills for non-developer workflows, a Sites preview that lets teams build and share hosted internal apps via URL, and Annotations for in-place document editing. With 5M weekly users and non-developers growing 3x faster than engineers, OpenAI is clearly repositioning Codex as a general enterprise automation platform, not just a coding tool.

report.title: OpenAI changes container session billing to per-minute starting June 2, ships Secure MCP Tunnel
report.summary: OpenAI moved container sessions from a flat 20-minute billing block to per-minute with a 5-minute minimum, cutting effective costs for short tasks. The same week, Secure MCP Tunnel shipped for enterprise customers, letting Codex and the Responses API connect to private on-prem MCP servers without exposing them to the public internet.

report.title: Anthropic launches Claude Partner Network Services Track and Partner Hub with 40K+ applicants
report.summary: Anthropic formalized its partner ecosystem on June 3 with a three-tier Services Track (Select, Preferred, Global Premier) and a public Partner Hub portal. Over 40,000 firms have applied and 10,000 consultants are certified; Deloitte, KPMG, Accenture, Cognizant, and PwC are already deploying Claude at scale. The move pairs the IPO filing and signals Anthropic is building the enterprise distribution layer before going public.

report.title: Microsoft's Project Polaris to replace GPT-4 Turbo in GitHub Copilot by August 2026
report.summary: Microsoft unveiled Project Polaris — a mixture-of-experts model with sub-modules tuned per programming language — as the new default reasoning engine for GitHub Copilot subscribers starting August 2026, with an optional three-month GPT-4 fallback. Microsoft now controls the model, inference, and developer experience end-to-end, cutting the commercial dependency on OpenAI for its flagship coding product.

report.title: Anthropic run-rate revenue surpasses $30B, enterprise clients spending $1M+ doubles to 1,000
report.summary: Anthropic disclosed that its annual run-rate revenue has surpassed $30 billion, up from roughly $9 billion at end of 2025, and that the number of business customers each spending over $1M annually has doubled to more than 1,000 in under two months. Claude Code's dominance in enterprise coding is the primary driver.

learn.name: Microsoft Agent Framework 1.0
learn.oneLineDescription: MIT-licensed Python/.NET SDK for building and deploying production multi-agent workflows.

detail.whatItDoes:
Microsoft Agent Framework (MAF) 1.0 is an open-source Python and .NET library for building, orchestrating, and deploying multi-agent AI workflows. It unifies AutoGen's multi-agent conversation patterns with Semantic Kernel's production-grade state management, authentication, and plugin architecture into a single framework with graph-based execution. Agents are defined around a first-class 'harness' concept that bundles skills, context memory, and middleware as named, versioned constructs.

At Build 2026, MAF was highlighted as the core build layer of the Microsoft Foundry stack. Agents built with MAF can run locally, escalate to Windows 365 cloud nodes, deploy to Azure via `azd ai agent init`, or publish into Teams and Office 365 Copilot. The Foundry Agent Service (GA end of June 2026) provides the managed hosted runtime, with hypervisor-isolated sandboxes, per-agent Entra ID identity, sub-100ms cold starts, and zero idle cost.
detail.whoItsFor: Platform and backend engineers building production agent systems on Azure or Windows. Teams currently using AutoGen or Semantic Kernel who need a unified path from prototype to production without rewriting. Enterprise teams that need auditability, Entra ID identity, and OpenTelemetry tracing baked in from day one. Python-first teams can start locally; .NET teams get the same surface via NuGet.
pros: MIT-licensed with active Microsoft engineering backing and a published v1.0 GA release (April 2, 2026)
Framework-agnostic deployment: the same agent manifest runs locally, on Windows 365, or in Azure Foundry Agent Service without rewrites
First-class observability: built-in OpenTelemetry, Azure Monitor integration, and Foundry tracing reach GA end of June 2026
Supports concurrent, handoff, and group-chat multi-agent workflow patterns out of the box
MCP server support for external tool integration; connectors for Azure OpenAI, standard OpenAI, and GitHub Copilot SDK
cons: Hosted Foundry Agent Service billing is per-invocation and per-tool-call; high-volume workloads should audit costs under the new AI Credits model before going to production
The framework is still maturing: several advanced features (Agent Optimizer, Adaptive Evaluations, incoming A2A) are in public preview rather than GA
detail.setupGuideMarkdown:
## Prerequisites
- Python 3.10+ (or .NET 10 for C#)
- Azure subscription (optional for local dev; required for hosted Foundry deployment)
- An OpenAI-compatible API key or Azure OpenAI endpoint

## Python quickstart

```bash
# Install the framework
pip install agent-framework

# Set your model credentials
export OPENAI_API_KEY="sk-..."
```

```python
# minimal_agent.py
from agent_framework import Agent

agent = Agent(
    name="ResearchAgent",
    model="gpt-4o",          # or "azure/gpt-4o" for Azure OpenAI
    instructions="Help users research topics. Be concise and cite sources."
)

response = agent.run("Summarize the key announcements from Microsoft Build 2026.")
print(response)
```

## .NET quickstart

```bash
# Add the NuGet package (v1.7.0 as of Build 2026)
dotnet add package Microsoft.Agents.AI
```

```csharp
// Program.cs
using Microsoft.Agents.AI;

var agent = new Agent(new AgentConfig
{
    Name = "ResearchAgent",
    Model = "gpt-4o",
    Instructions = "Help users research topics."
});

var response = await agent.RunAsync("What shipped at Build 2026?");
Console.WriteLine(response);
```

## Multi-agent workflow (Python)

```python
from agent_framework import Agent, Handoff

writer = Agent(
    name="Writer",
    model="gpt-4o",
    instructions="Write a first draft based on the user's brief."
)

editor = Agent(
    name="Editor",
    model="gpt-4o",
    instructions="Improve clarity and remove jargon from the writer's draft.",
    handoffs=[Handoff(from_agent="Writer")]
)

# Run the pipeline
result = writer.run("Write a short blog post about agentic AI in 2026.")
final  = editor.run(result)
print(final)
```

## Deploy to Azure Foundry Agent Service

```bash
# Requires Azure Developer CLI (azd)
npm install -g @azure/azd     # or: winget install Microsoft.Azd

cd your-agent-project
azd ai agent init             # scaffolds agent.json manifest
azd deploy                    # source-code deploy, no container required
```

**Gotcha:** Foundry Agent Service billing switched to the AI Credits model on June 1, 2026. Run `azd ai agent cost-estimate` before deploying high-frequency agents to avoid surprise invoices. Local dev is always free.

learn.name: OpenAI Codex CLI
learn.oneLineDescription: Open-source terminal coding agent: assigns tasks, writes code, runs tests, opens PRs autonomously.

detail.whatItDoes:
OpenAI Codex CLI is an open-source command-line coding agent that runs locally in your terminal. It accepts natural-language task descriptions, writes code, runs tests in a sandboxed environment, and can open PRs against your repo. Each session runs inside a secure sandbox with configurable network access (package registries only, full internet, or specific-domain allowlists). The Python SDK now ships with a first-class `CodexConfig` API and supports async workflows; sessions can be archived, resumed, and forked.

As of June 2026, the CLI reached full production status with 5M+ weekly users. The latest updates add session archiving (`/archive`, `codex archive`), TUI markdown with clickable OSC 8 links, remote execution via `CODEX_API_KEY`, and a feature-gated image generation extension. Memory summaries are versioned and auto-rebuilt to keep long-lived contexts lean. The Python SDK can now be staged and published independently from runtime releases using `python-v*` tags.
detail.whoItsFor: Individual developers and small teams who want async background coding tasks. Particularly effective for batching maintenance work (dependency updates, test coverage, documentation fixes) that would otherwise consume 30-40% of a developer's day. Also useful for non-developers (analysts, researchers) who can describe outcomes in plain English and let Codex handle the implementation via role-specific plugins.
pros: Fully open-source (MIT) with active weekly releases; the Python SDK supports API-key, ChatGPT browser, and device-code auth flows
Configurable sandbox network access: choose package-registry-only, full internet, or a per-domain allowlist depending on your security posture
Goal mode (now GA across app, IDE extension, and CLI) lets you define a success criterion and let Codex keep iterating until it's met
Integrates with Netlify, Vercel, Cloudflare, Figma, and Salesforce natively; MCP server support for custom tool connections
cons: Remote execution still requires an approved OpenAI host for CODEX_API_KEY registration — you cannot point it at an arbitrary self-hosted endpoint yet
Container session costs: billed per-minute with a 5-minute minimum as of June 2, 2026; long-running autonomous tasks can accumulate charges quickly if you are not monitoring session duration
detail.setupGuideMarkdown:
## Prerequisites
- Node 20+ (for the npm install path) **or** Rust toolchain (for build-from-source)
- An OpenAI API key (`OPENAI_API_KEY`), or a ChatGPT Plus/Business subscription for browser auth

## Install

```bash
# Recommended: npm global install (macOS/Linux/Windows)
npm install -g openai-codex

# Verify install and check system prerequisites
codex doctor
```

```bash
# Alternative: pip install (Python SDK beta)
pip install openai-codex
```

## Authenticate

```bash
# Option 1: API key (fastest)
export OPENAI_API_KEY="sk-..."

# Option 2: ChatGPT browser flow (no API key needed)
codex auth login --flow browser

# Option 3: Device code (for headless environments)
codex auth login --flow device
```

## Run your first task

```bash
# Inside any git repo
cd your-project

# Describe a task in plain English
codex "Add input validation to the /signup endpoint and write unit tests"

# Watch it work in the TUI; approve or reject the proposed changes
```

## Configure sandbox network access

```toml
# ~/.codex/config.toml
[sandbox]
# Options: "package_registries" | "full_internet" | "specific_domains"
network_access = "package_registries"
allowed_domains = []  # populate if using "specific_domains"

[git]
# Attribute commits to Codex (requires codex_git_commit = true)
codex_git_commit = true
```

## Goal mode (define success criteria)

```bash
# Let Codex keep iterating until tests pass
codex goal "All existing tests pass and coverage is above 80%" --max-iterations 10
```

## Archive a session

```bash
# From TUI
/archive

# From CLI
codex archive <session-id>
codex unarchive <session-id>   # restore when needed
```

**Gotcha:** The `--full-auto` flag was deprecated. Use explicit permission profiles instead (`--permission-profile trusted` or `--permission-profile sandboxed`). Old scripts using `--full-auto` will warn and fall back to the sandboxed profile.

learn.name: Microsoft Agent Governance Toolkit
learn.oneLineDescription: MIT-licensed policy enforcement and audit layer for autonomous AI agents — covers all 10 OWASP Agentic AI risks.

detail.whatItDoes:
The Microsoft Agent Governance Toolkit is an open-source, MIT-licensed runtime security layer for autonomous AI agents. It enforces deterministic policies at sub-millisecond latency (<0.1ms p99), covering all 10 OWASP Agentic AI Top 10 risks: goal hijacking, tool misuse, identity abuse, memory poisoning, cascading failures, and rogue agents. The toolkit is structured as a monorepo with seven independently installable packages — you can start with just the policy engine and add identity management, sandboxing, and SRE tooling as your agent system grows.

It integrates natively with LangChain, CrewAI, Google ADK, Microsoft Agent Framework, OpenAI Agents SDK, Haystack, LangGraph, and PydanticAI by hooking into each framework's native extension points. A TypeScript SDK (`@microsoft/agentmesh-sdk`) and a .NET NuGet package (`Microsoft.AgentGovernance`) cover Node.js and C# teams. The toolkit also maps agent behavior to EU AI Act, HIPAA, and SOC2 compliance requirements and generates evidence collection reports.
detail.whoItsFor: Platform and security engineers deploying agents to production who need auditable, tamper-evident records of every agent decision. Compliance-sensitive industries (healthcare, finance, legal) where HIPAA, SOC2, or the EU AI Act (enforcement starts August 2026) require provable controls. Teams running multi-agent systems where a single API key is shared across five agents and 'an agent did it' is not an acceptable incident response.
pros: Sub-millisecond policy enforcement (<0.1ms p99) — governance adds no perceptible latency to agent tool calls
Framework-agnostic: integrates via native extension points, not wrappers; adding governance does not require rewriting agent code
Covers all 10 OWASP Agentic AI Top 10 risks with deterministic controls, not prompt-level guardrails
Incremental adoption: seven independently installable packages; start with just the policy engine
cons: Azure-hosted deployment path (AKS sidecar, Foundry middleware, Container Apps) assumes familiarity with Azure infrastructure; purely local setups require more manual configuration
The plugin marketplace (Agent Marketplace component) uses Ed25519 signing and trust-tiered capability gating — correct setup requires understanding the key management flow before going to production
detail.setupGuideMarkdown:
## Prerequisites
- Python 3.10+
- An agent built with any supported framework (LangChain, LangGraph, OpenAI Agents SDK, CrewAI, MAF, etc.)
- (Optional) Azure subscription for AKS or Container Apps deployment

## Install

```bash
# Core policy engine only (lightest starting point)
pip install microsoft-agent-governance

# Full suite (policy + identity + sandboxing + SRE + compliance + marketplace + lightning)
pip install microsoft-agent-governance[full]

# TypeScript / Node.js
npm install @microsoft/agentmesh-sdk

# .NET
dotnet add package Microsoft.AgentGovernance
```

## Minimal Python integration (LangChain)

```python
from agent_governance import PolicyEngine, GovernanceConfig
from langchain.agents import initialize_agent

# Define a policy: block drop_table even if the model requests it
policy = PolicyEngine(
    config=GovernanceConfig(
        denied_tools=["drop_table", "delete_all_records"],
        require_audit_log=True,
        audit_log_path="./agent_audit.jsonl"
    )
)

# Wrap your existing LangChain agent
@policy.enforce
def run_agent(query: str):
    agent = initialize_agent(tools, llm, agent="zero-shot-react-description")
    return agent.run(query)

result = run_agent("Summarize the sales report for Q1 2026")
```

## Identity isolation for multi-agent systems

```python
from agent_governance.identity import AgentIdentityManager

# Give each agent its own identity and audit trail
identity_mgr = AgentIdentityManager()

research_agent_id = identity_mgr.register("ResearchAgent", capabilities=["web_search", "read_file"])
billing_agent_id  = identity_mgr.register("BillingAgent",  capabilities=["query_database"])

# Now every tool call is attributed to a specific agent, not a shared API key
```

## Clone and explore the full repo

```bash
git clone https://github.com/microsoft/agent-governance-toolkit
cd agent-governance-toolkit

# Run example: policy enforcement demo
python examples/policy_enforcement_demo.py

# Run compliance report against EU AI Act
python examples/compliance_report.py --framework eu-ai-act
```

## Azure AKS sidecar deployment

```bash
# Deploy as a sidecar alongside your existing agent container
# Full step-by-step in the repo's /deploy/aks directory
git clone https://github.com/microsoft/agent-governance-toolkit
cd agent-governance-toolkit/deploy/aks

# Edit values.yaml with your agent image and policy config
helm install agent-governance ./chart -f values.yaml
```

**Gotcha:** The EU AI Act's high-risk AI obligations take effect in August 2026 and the Colorado AI Act becomes enforceable in June 2026. If you deploy agents in regulated contexts, run `python -m agent_governance compliance-check --standard eu-ai-act` before launch — it outputs a gap report with evidence collection instructions.

learn.name: OpenClaw
learn.oneLineDescription: Local-first AI personal agent with 50+ integrations (WhatsApp, Slack, iMessage) that writes its own skills.

detail.whatItDoes: OpenClaw is an open-source local AI assistant and agent gateway. It runs entirely on your own device and connects AI models to over 50 integrations including WhatsApp, Telegram, Slack, Discord, Signal, and iMessage. Unlike cloud-based assistants, all data stays on your machine. The assistant runs persistently in the background and can browse the web, fill out forms, run shell commands, write and execute code, and control desktop apps. Its standout capability: it can write new skills for itself, extending its own functionality without manual developer intervention. Originally created by PSPDFKit founder Peter Steinberger, it went viral in January 2026 (9K to 210K+ stars in weeks) and has since transitioned to an open-source foundation after Steinberger joined OpenAI.
detail.whoItsFor: Developers and power users who want a fully private, always-on AI agent without sending data to cloud APIs. Teams with strict data sovereignty requirements. Anyone building personal automation workflows across messaging platforms without writing custom integrations. Security-conscious individuals who want local inference via Ollama or llama.cpp as the model backend.
pros: All data stays on your machine — no cloud API required if paired with Ollama or another local inference backend
50+ messaging and productivity integrations available out of the box with no custom API connection work
Self-extending: the agent writes new skill modules for itself based on observed user workflows
210K+ GitHub stars with an active open-source foundation maintaining it post-Steinberger
cons: Requires broad OS permissions (shell access, contacts, browser control) — the permission surface is wide and security researchers have flagged that the community skill repository lacks rigorous vetting for malicious submissions
Self-written skills can behave unpredictably; production or enterprise use requires careful sandboxing and skill auditing before deployment
detail.setupGuideMarkdown:
## Prerequisites
- macOS (primary), Linux (beta), or Windows (via WSL2)
- Node 20+ and npm
- Optional but recommended: [Ollama](https://ollama.com) for local model inference (no API key needed)

## Install

```bash
# Clone the repo
git clone https://github.com/openclaw-ai/openclaw
cd openclaw

# Install dependencies
npm install

# Copy the example config
cp config.example.json config.json
```

## Configure a model backend

```json
// config.json — local inference via Ollama (no API key)
{
  "model": {
    "provider": "ollama",
    "name": "llama3.1:8b",
    "base_url": "http://localhost:11434"
  }
}
```

```json
// config.json — cloud inference via OpenAI
{
  "model": {
    "provider": "openai",
    "name": "gpt-4o",
    "api_key": "sk-..."
  }
}
```

## Start Ollama (if using local inference)

```bash
# Install Ollama first: https://ollama.com/download
ollama pull llama3.1:8b
ollama serve        # runs on localhost:11434 by default
```

## Launch OpenClaw

```bash
npm run start
# OpenClaw starts in the background and opens a tray icon
# Access the dashboard at http://localhost:3000
```

## Add an integration (example: Slack)

```bash
# From the dashboard -> Integrations -> Slack
# Follow the OAuth flow, then test:
npx openclaw test-integration slack
```

## Write a custom skill manually

```javascript
// skills/summarize-slack-channel.js
module.exports = {
  name: 'summarize-slack-channel',
  description: 'Summarizes the last N messages in a Slack channel',
  parameters: { channel: 'string', count: 'number' },
  async run({ channel, count }, { integrations }) {
    const messages = await integrations.slack.getMessages(channel, count);
    return messages.map(m => `${m.user}: ${m.text}`).join('\n');
  }
};
```

**Gotcha:** The community skill repository (`skills/community/`) is not centrally reviewed. Before installing any community skill, read its source — a malicious skill with shell access can exfiltrate files. Stick to first-party skills or skills you've read yourself until the foundation ships a formal review process.

learn.name: AI Foundry for Windows SDK
learn.oneLineDescription: Single NuGet package bundling ONNX Runtime, DirectML, and Copilot Runtime for on-device Windows AI agents.

detail.whatItDoes:
The AI Foundry for Windows SDK, shipped at Build 2026, is a single NuGet package (`Microsoft.AI.Foundry.Local.WinML`) that bundles the ONNX Runtime, DirectML, and the Windows Copilot Runtime together. Previously, wiring up on-device AI on Windows required managing three separate libraries with incompatible versioning. The SDK auto-targets whatever compute is available: NPU on Copilot+ PCs, GPU on gaming rigs, CPU everywhere else. No Azure subscription, no API keys, no per-token cost — data stays on device. Minimum bar is Windows 10/11 x64 with 8GB RAM; 16GB is comfortable for larger models.

The SDK is the local runtime layer of the broader Windows Agent Framework. It supports C#, JavaScript, Python, and Rust. Agents built locally can be promoted to Azure Foundry Agent Service using the same `agent.json` manifest without rewrites — making it the lowest-friction path to local-first agent development on Windows.
detail.whoItsFor: Windows and .NET developers who want to run AI inference on-device without Azure costs or cloud dependencies. Enterprise teams with data residency requirements that prevent sending data to any cloud API. Game developers, productivity tool builders, and Copilot+ PC ISVs targeting Microsoft's new agent distribution channel (Windows Agent Store). Teams who want to prototype locally and deploy to Azure later without changing their code.
pros: Zero cloud cost for local execution — no API keys, no per-token billing, no Azure subscription required
Single package replaces three previously separate libraries (ONNX Runtime, DirectML, Copilot Runtime) with one versioned install
Hardware auto-targeting: NPU on Copilot+ PCs, GPU on gaming machines, CPU fallback everywhere else — no hardware-specific code branches
Same agent.json manifest works locally and in Azure Foundry Agent Service — no rewrites when scaling out
cons: Windows 10/11 x64 only; no macOS or Linux support — cross-platform teams cannot share the same local inference path
Larger models require 16GB+ RAM and a recent GPU or NPU for comfortable performance; 8GB minimum systems will hit latency limits on anything beyond a 3B parameter model
detail.setupGuideMarkdown:
## Prerequisites
- Windows 10 or Windows 11 (x64)
- 8 GB RAM minimum; 16 GB recommended
- .NET 8+ or .NET 10 (for C# projects)
- Optional: Copilot+ PC (Snapdragon X, AMD Strix, or Intel Lunar Lake) for NPU acceleration

## Install Foundry Local (winget)

```powershell
# Install the Foundry Local runtime (already GA before Build 2026)
winget install Microsoft.FoundryLocal

# Verify
foundry-local --version
```

## Add the SDK to your .NET project

```bash
# Core agent SDK
dotnet add package Microsoft.Agents.AI

# On-device WinML inference layer (the new Build 2026 package)
dotnet add package Microsoft.AI.Foundry.Local.WinML
```

## Minimal C# on-device agent

```csharp
using Microsoft.Agents.AI;
using Microsoft.AI.Foundry.Local.WinML;

// Auto-selects NPU > GPU > CPU based on available hardware
var localModel = await WinMLModelLoader.LoadAsync("phi-3.5-mini");

var agent = new Agent(new AgentConfig
{
    Name        = "LocalResearchAgent",
    ModelClient = localModel,   // runs entirely on-device
    Instructions = "Answer questions concisely using only local knowledge."
});

var response = await agent.RunAsync("Summarize the risks of agentic AI.");
Console.WriteLine(response);
// No network call made — data never leaves the machine
```

## Download a model for local use

```powershell
# List available on-device models
foundry-local model list

# Pull a model (stored in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\FoundryLocal\models)
foundry-local model pull phi-3.5-mini
foundry-local model pull llama-3.2-3b
```

## Promote local agent to Azure Foundry Agent Service

```bash
# When you're ready to scale out, the same manifest works in Azure
azd ai agent init   # generates agent.json from your local config
azd deploy          # no container required — source-code deploy
```

**Gotcha:** The `WinML` package requires the Windows Copilot Runtime, which ships in Windows 11 24H2 and later. On Windows 10 or older Windows 11 builds, you need to install the runtime separately via `winget install Microsoft.CopilotRuntime`. Running `foundry-local doctor` will flag this and give you the exact install command.
